memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text: "He shall then slaughter the goat for the sin offering for the people and take its blood behind the curtain and do with it as he did with the bull's blood: He shall sprinkle it on the atonement cover and in front of it." - Lev 16:15 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
Now the goat's blood, for the people. The same curtain, the same cover, the same sprinkling.

Notice how the day is structured. Aaron for himself. Then Aaron for everyone. Every Israelite — the faithful and the careless, the elderly widow and the rebellious teenager, those who had come to the tabernacle all year and those who had not — all covered by the same blood on the same day.

Nobody's name was read out. Nobody was assessed individually. The high priest went in as their representative, and what he did there counted for all of them.

That is the logic Paul uses about Christ. Just as one trespass resulted in condemnation for all people, so also one righteous act resulted in justification and life for all who receive it (Rom 5:18-19). One man acting on behalf of many.

The Israelites outside were not doing anything to secure this. They were waiting. Their standing before God depended entirely on what someone else was doing on their behalf, out of sight.

That is where your salvation rests too. Not on your performance today, but on what Christ has already done in your place.

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
1. Do you try to secure your standing with God by your own efforts?
2. What does it mean that Christ acted on your behalf, not you?
3. How does representation change the way you view your bad days?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text: Father, thank You that my standing before You rests on what Christ has done in my place, not on my performance. Let me rest in His finished work today. Amen.
